channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Uzbeks in trouble abroad to get help through the Online Mahalla platform
item.description: At a 2 November meeting the president put special focus on protecting the rights of citizens abroad: those in difficulty can leave a message on the Online Mahalla platform, and ambassadors will personally take up the case when needed; the system launches within 10 days.

item.title: Mirziyoyev orders overhaul of labour migration: 'We need quality, not numbers'
item.description: At a 2 November meeting the president ordered better public awareness of overseas jobs, a migration centre in every region, and vocational and German-language training for young people; Germany requested 45,000 specialists but hired only 2,000.

item.title: The 1944 Deportation of the Meskhetian Turks to Central Asia: Life in Uzbekistan and the Blocked Road Home
item.description: In November 1944 Stalin's regime deported the Meskhetian Turks, Kurds, and Hemshils from the Meskheti region of Georgia on the Turkish border to Central Asia. Roughly 90,000-115,000 people were removed, and tens of thousands died in transit and in the first years. Here is the documented history of their homeland, the deportation order, life under the special-settlement regime in Uzbekistan, and the return to Georgia that stayed closed.

item.title: North Korea tests cluster warhead for tactical ballistic missiles
item.description: Pyongyang said its "Type-2 standard" cluster warhead could devastate a target area of about 12–13 hectares; the test was guided by Central Military Commission member Kim Jong-sik.

item.title: Sunni and Shia Islam: Their Differences, Historical Origins, and Schools
item.description: Islam's two main branches — Sunni and Shia — grew out of the question of who should lead the community after the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Here are the history of that split, the main theological and legal differences, the schools, the rough global distribution, and the situation in Uzbekistan and Central Asia — set out neutrally and respectfully.

item.title: How the World Trade Organization (WTO) Works and Uzbekistan's Membership: An Explainer
item.description: The WTO is the international body that sets the rules of world trade, built on tariff reduction and non-discrimination. Here is how it was created, how it is structured, how it settles disputes, and where Uzbekistan's accession bid — ongoing since 1994 — now stands.

item.title: Qatar-mediated US–Iran talks continue in Doha: what we know
item.description: Iranian negotiators met Qatari mediators in Doha for a third day; Trump said the talks were "going fine," while Iran favoured diplomacy but said it was ready to respond to any attack.

item.title: Ziroat Mirziyoyeva proposes girls' education initiatives at OTS Family and Women Council
item.description: The Organization of Turkic States' Council on Family and Women met for the first time in Ankara; Uzbekistan's First Lady proposed initiatives on girls' education, women's entrepreneurship and family support.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Japan: Diplomatic Ties and Aid (1992–1996)
item.description: In the first years of independence, Uzbekistan and Japan established official relations. Japan's recognition of Uzbekistan's independence, the exact date of diplomatic relations, the embassies, Japan's role as a major donor through ODA (Official Development Assistance) and JICA, the early loans, and President Islam Karimov's 1994 visit are set out from the sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan adopts Islamic finance roadmap: 2026–2030, 39 measures
item.description: The Central Bank approved a roadmap of five areas and 39 measures; 11 microfinance organizations already offer interest-free services, and Open Bank received the first Islamic banking licence.

item.title: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3bn crypto theft from Binance
item.description: The FBI tied the theft to North Korea's "TraderTraitor" group; Binance covered 90% of the losses and resumed withdrawals.

item.title: Uzbekistan issues its first Islamic banking licence: Open Bank and a $1bn plan
item.description: On October 23 the Central Bank granted Open Bank the country's first Islamic banking licence. Here is the legal basis, the permitted Shariah-compliant services and the state's 2026–2030 attraction plan — verified facts only.

item.title: Ecological Migration: The Aral Sea Disaster and the Exodus from Karakalpakstan
item.description: The drying of the Aral Sea was not only a natural catastrophe but a human one: as the fishery collapsed and the air and water turned toxic, tens of thousands left their homeland in Karakalpakstan. Here is the history, the figures, and the present state of this "ecological migration".

item.title: Islam Makhachev: 'My next fight is one of the last in my career'
item.description: UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev spoke on October 31 about his retirement plan. His record, his last fight and his next opponent — verified facts only.

item.title: How Waqf (an Islamic Endowment) Works: An Explainer
item.description: A waqf is a way of dedicating property permanently to a charitable or public purpose: the underlying asset is preserved while the income it generates flows continuously to a good cause. Here is how it is set up, its main types, its historical role, and why it matters for Uzbekistan.

item.title: Estate Planning in the US: How Wills, Trusts, and Probate Work
item.description: Wills, living trusts, probate, beneficiary designations, and powers of attorney — the basics of the US inheritance system for immigrant families. This is general information, not legal advice; rules vary from state to state.

item.title: 'Muslims burned five churches in France' is fake news, fact-checkers find
item.description: A France 24 Observers and Observatory for Religious Heritage check: no church fire during the October 17 unrest was linked to Muslims. Here is how the false claim spread, who spread it and what actually happened — verified facts only.

item.title: US moves to deport Afghan refugees to Pakistan: the Qatar camp and the Taliban risk
item.description: The US administration is preparing to send Afghan refugees to Pakistan, with a first flight possible as early as Monday. The camp figures, the return risk and the timeline — verified facts only.

item.title: The Establishment of Diplomatic Relations Between Uzbekistan and Germany (1991–1996)
item.description: Germany was among the first Western countries to recognize independent Uzbekistan. From the recognition of 31 December 1991 to the formal relations of 6 March 1992 and the economic and cultural cooperation of the early years — the story of an important door the young state opened to Europe.

item.title: Bangsamoro elects its first chief minister: former rebel Abdulraof Macacua takes office
item.description: The parliament of the Philippines' autonomous Muslim-majority region chose Abdulraof Macacua as its first elected chief minister on October 30. Who he is, the vote figures and what it means — verified facts only.

item.title: How Sukuk (Islamic Bonds) Work: An Explainer
item.description: Sukuk are an Islamic finance instrument built on ownership of a real asset and profit-sharing instead of interest (riba). Here is how they differ from ordinary bonds, their main structures, and why they matter for Uzbekistan.

item.title: Saudi ambassador compares the Houthis to ISIS, calls for a broad coalition
item.description: Saudi Arabia's ambassador to the US, Princess Reema bint Bandar Al Saud, compared the Houthis to ISIS in a New York Times op-ed published after a deadly attack on Riyadh's airport.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 1.1mn citizens returned from abroad in 9M26, 172,000 found permanent jobs
item.description: More than 1.1 million Uzbeks returned from abroad in January–September 2026. According to the Ministry of Employment, 172,000 found permanent jobs and 349,000 became self-employed, but 257,000 remain unemployed.

item.title: Uzbekistan and the European Union: The Partnership and Cooperation Agreement (1996) and the First Years
item.description: In the early years of independence Uzbekistan laid the foundations of formal ties with Europe. From the 1992 memorandum to the Partnership and Cooperation Agreement signed in Florence in 1996 — the dates and facts of the first European diplomacy.

item.title: Israel's election ends without a majority; Germany reacts cautiously
item.description: In the October 27 Knesset election no bloc reached 61 seats; Netanyahu's bloc took 53 and the opposition 48. Germany is withholding judgment until a coalition is clear.

item.title: Uzbek Labour Migration to Poland: The Rise of a New European Destination
item.description: Over the past decade Poland has become one of the most important European destinations for Uzbek labour migrants. The war in Ukraine, Poland's labour shortage, and Uzbekistan's diversification policy shaped this new wave — with the numbers.

item.title: How a U.S. Credit Score Works: FICO, VantageScore, and How to Improve It
item.description: In the U.S., renting an apartment, an auto loan, a mortgage — even a job — can hinge on your credit score. Here is how the 300–850 FICO and VantageScore are calculated, which factors weigh most, and how a newcomer builds a score from zero.

item.title: Uzbekistan's poverty rate fell from 5.8% to 3.6% in nine months — Employment Ministry
item.description: According to the Ministry of Employment and Poverty Reduction's nine-month 2026 results, the poverty rate fell from 5.8% to 3.6% and 824,000 people were placed in permanent jobs.

item.title: IISS: Gulf states must rethink their trillion-dollar defence after the war
item.description: According to the IISS Strategic Dossier "The Gulf at War," the 2026 war exposed the weakness of the Gulf states' US-weapons-reliant defence.

item.title: Uzbekistan sets up nuclear classes at two Tashkent academic lyceums — Uzatom
item.description: The Tashkent branch of the MEPhI nuclear university is opening specialised nuclear classes at the I. M. Gubkin and International House-Tashkent academic lyceums to prepare students for the country's nuclear energy sector.
